# v0.24.0-rc3 — hermes-lcm-x: catalog identity (BREAKING rename) and in-place compaction fix release candidate

**RELEASE CANDIDATE — not GA.** This prerelease enters the RELEASE-READINESS-V1 gauntlet
(bench/specs/RELEASE-READINESS-V1.md): Phase A (all-tools live matrix on a fresh clone across
privacy postures, planted-secret battery), Phase B (multi-agent P0/P1 sweep of the previous-GA→rc
diff, v0.23.3→this candidate, including the upgrade and migration path), Phase C (30+ turn live
session soak). GA follows only with all three receipts green, and the GA tree is this tree plus the
release-notes file. This is a feature train: the GA cut is the owner's.

**BREAKING.** The plugin is renamed `hermes-lcm` → `hermes-lcm-x` and the context engine `lcm` →
`lcm-x`, so LCM-X can enter the Hermes plugin catalog under its own identity (#471). An in-place
update with an unchanged config stops loading LCM-X; follow the migration steps below before
restarting Hermes. The store (`lcm.db`), the `lcm:` config block, `LCM_*` environment variables,
the 15 `lcm_*` tools, `/lcm` and the "LCM plugin loaded" log line are unchanged. No default and no
privacy posture changed.

## Changes since v0.24.0-rc2 (#483, #484, #486)

Hermes in-place compaction (`compression.in_place`, on by default) commits a compaction by calling the
context engine's session-end hook with the pre-compaction message list, then restarting the same session
id. Up to rc2, and on v0.23.x, LCM-X treated that call as a real session end. It finalized the session,
which reset the published frontier to 0, so every later compaction in that session was refused as a
publication-invariant conflict. It also re-ingested the pre-compaction list, writing duplicate rows
(about 50 per turn on a live profile) (#483).

- Each `compress()` call records a proof: the exact message identities it received and returned, bound to
  its session and conversation. A session end whose messages equal that input is a compaction commit: it
  finalizes with the session's own frontier but does not re-ingest. The following same-id compression start
  restores that frontier and keeps the ingest position. A finalize now records only the finalizing session's
  own frontier, so a session sharing a conversation never inherits another session's frontier.
- The ingest position is kept only when the host's next list matches the proof. Otherwise the existing
  reconciliation runs, preferring a visible duplicate over a silently skipped message. A host that merges
  the summary into a user turn is recognized only when the merged text matches one of this session's stored
  summaries exactly.
- The proof is also written to `lcm.db` as one metadata row per compacted session, with no schema change.
  A restart or a session rotation therefore resumes at the proven position.
- The same fix covers rotation (`compression.in_place: false`). On rc2, the real-host harness showed rotation
  runs losing user turns and replies after the second compaction. On rc3, with native recovery off, every in-place
  and rotation run commits all compactions with nothing missing and no duplicate rows. A restart after a completed compaction and before
  the next message reads the proof back from `lcm.db`, also for a rotated session with no messages yet (a crash between a rotation's parent
  end and child start is not covered: #489).
- No replay match relies on a message whose stored form is lossy by design (password redaction), in the proof
  checks, native recovery, or the older end-of-session reconciliation. Every reconciliation path skips a summary
  merged into a user turn only when it matches one of the session's own stored summaries exactly; any other summary-shaped text is
  stored as content (#486).

## Changes since v0.24.0-rc1 (#477, #478)

- The `identity_migration` notice leads with stop Hermes → edit `config.yaml` → start Hermes; a new
  `steps` list wraps the unchanged rc1 `change` list, and the live-edit fallback is named when the `lcm`
  alias is active. README/operator-guide step 4: `hermes-lcm-x` enabled, `hermes-lcm` not enabled.

## Rename with a migration path (#471, #472)

- `plugin.yaml` is `name: hermes-lcm-x`; the engine reports `lcm-x`. One module
  (`plugin_identity.py`) owns every produced or compared name.
- The legacy `context.engine: lcm` still selects LCM-X through an alias, with a once-per-process
  `DEPRECATED LCM-X config` warning, an `identity_migration` field in `lcm_status`, and an
  `identity_migration` `warn` check in `lcm_doctor`.
- What cannot be aliased: Hermes matches `plugins.enabled` against the manifest name before any
  plugin code runs. A config that enables only `hermes-lcm` logs `Context engine 'lcm' not found —
  falling back to built-in compressor` and runs without LCM-X. `lcm.db` is untouched, but turns
  handled in that state are not in `lcm.db`.
- Two installed copies cannot both write the store: the second generation logs `Another LCM
  generation is already loaded` and stays inert.
- `scripts/install.sh` installs to `plugins/hermes-lcm-x`, reuses an existing `plugins/hermes-lcm`
  checkout of the same tree, prints the migration steps when it finds a legacy install or config,
  and never edits `config.yaml` or deletes anything.

Migration (one LCM copy; change the config while Hermes is stopped):

1. Stop Hermes; check out this candidate in the existing clone (`git fetch --tags && git checkout
   v0.24.0-rc3`) or a new checkout, then run `scripts/install.sh`. A clone that tracks `main` with
   `git pull --ff-only` gets the current `main`, not necessarily this candidate.
2. In `plugins.enabled` replace `hermes-lcm` with `hermes-lcm-x`; set `context.engine: lcm-x`.
3. Start Hermes; check that `hermes plugins` lists `hermes-lcm-x` and the log shows `LCM plugin
   loaded — lossless context management active`.

Managed fleets (PCS / managed-plugin payloads) stay pinned to v0.23.x until their own config
migration stages `hermes-lcm-x`.

## Hermes plugin-catalog admission (#473)

- `post_llm_call` registers through `ctx.register_hook` when the host provides it; hosts without it
  keep the direct `PluginManager._hooks` fallback. `plugin.yaml` declares the four hooks registered on
  the public-hook path (`pre_llm_call`, `post_llm_call`, `subagent_start`, `subagent_stop`).
- `scripts/update.sh` is removed (catalog rule: no self-updater). Branch checkouts update with
  `git pull --ff-only` + `scripts/install.sh`; a tag checkout (migration step 1) updates with
  `git fetch --tags && git checkout <tag>` + `scripts/install.sh`; catalog installs with
  `hermes plugins update hermes-lcm-x`.
- Install-scanner findings neutralized with no behavior change (PEM markers built from constants,
  env capture without an `env` pipe, one comment reworded); the README lists every remaining
  informational finding with a reason. No `caution` or `dangerous` findings remain.
- `FINDINGS-VERDICTS-*.md` moved to `docs/history/`.

## Governance: required AI review check retired (#474, #475)

The required `AI review exact-head` check and its v2 receipt gate are retired: no publisher ever
emitted the v2 marker, and every merge after it landed through a ruleset transition. Enforcement is
strict exact-head CI (six checks), required review-thread resolution and merge commits only. AI
review is recorded evidence plus a `land-pr` obligation (acceptance review on every PR; acceptance
plus a distinct adversarial review from a different model on memory-preservation and review-policy
paths; a pointer-only merge receipt). Maintainer-facing only; no product code.

## Known limitation (#488)

LCM-X reserves its rendered summary-block format. A user message that is, or begins with, a byte-exact copy of one of the
session's own summary blocks (header with node id, summary text and expand hint) can be taken for generated context by a
restart reconciliation and not stored. Copies from another session are refused; the whole-message case is the same on rc2.
Removing the limitation needs position evidence (#488). Whether GA waits for that fix is part of the GA decision.

## Known follow-ups (tracked, non-blocking)

- Managed fleets: staging `hermes-lcm-x` in fleet configs (PCS / managed-plugin payloads) is a separate
  fleet-migration change; fleets stay on v0.23.x until it lands.
- #380 — the privacy-posture flip (cloud-copy transform opt-in), ruled for "the next feature train",
  is not in this release; which train carries it is an open owner decision.
- #479 — opt-in `LCM_NATIVE_RECOVERY=true` aborts every compaction on Hermes v0.21.4 (a host
  stale-attempt check). The host fix (NousResearch/hermes-agent#121162) ships in Hermes v0.21.5 (`v2026.9.24`);
  older releases remain affected. Keep native recovery off (the default) regardless, because of #482 and #487.
- #482 — with `LCM_NATIVE_RECOVERY=true`, Hermes's own pruning can rewrite the protected tail, and LCM-X
  then rejects the host summary. This is another reason to keep native recovery off. LCM-X's own
  compaction (native recovery off) is the path this release fixes (#483).
- #487 — with native recovery on, host-native compactions still store some duplicate rows (unchanged from rc2;
  measured in the real-host harness). The fix (a commit proof for host-native adoption) ships together with the #482
  fix in the next native-recovery change.
- #489 — rotation: a crash between parent end and child start stores the parent's recent turns again (duplicates, no loss).
- #485 — rows duplicated by pre-fix compaction replays stay in `lcm.db`; detector and repair (never delete) tracked.
- Hermes plugin catalog: the `hermes-lcm-x` catalog entry is submitted after GA, pinned to the GA commit.

## Benchmark boundary

#484 changes ingest bookkeeping only on the Hermes compaction-commit path: which rows a session-end or
same-id compression start writes, and where ingestion resumes. Recall ranking, assembly and the privacy
transforms are unchanged. No benchmark instrument in `bench/` calls `compress()` or the session-end hook, so the banked rows keep
their commits of record and this train adds no ledger row. The rest of the
train is unchanged from rc2: #472 renames identities behind one constants module with a legacy alias,
#473 moves one hook registration onto the public `register_hook` API and rewrites scanner-flagged literals
with byte-identical values, #475 touches governance files only, and #478 changes only the migration notice text.

## Upgrade

Follow the migration steps above. This release makes no schema change: a `lcm.db` created by
v0.23.3 reopens on this tree with an identical logical dump, row counts and search hits. After the
first compaction it holds one extra metadata row per compacted session (the commit proof), which
v0.23.3 ignores.
Rollback: stop Hermes, check out v0.23.3, restore `plugins.enabled: [hermes-lcm]` and
`context.engine: lcm`. The store schema version is unchanged in this train (`db_bootstrap.py`
changes only message wording), so v0.23.3 opens the same `lcm.db`. The Phase B sweep exercises
the upgrade and this rollback.
